description: A stream whose first event is response.failed with a usage limit (error type usage_limit_reached) reaches the client as the usage limit's 429 before the stream starts, as when the limit comes as an HTTP 429, not as a 502.

error.message: The usage limit has been reached

exceptions.reason: The new core builds the client's error body itself, as for every upstream (decision in slice 1): a Codex usage_limit_reached failure becomes a 429 with code usage_limit_reached and type rate_limit_error, as when the limit comes as an HTTP 429. Today's core passes the upstream's error object through, with its resets_in_seconds.

want.message: The usage limit has been reached

exceptions.reason: Today's core copies the failed event's sequence_number into the error body it passes through; the new core builds the error body itself and the reply never started, so there is no stream position to report.
The new core sends the usage limit's reset time (resets_in_seconds) in Retry-After, as both cores do when the limit comes as an HTTP 429; today's core does not read it from a failed stream event.
The new core's Codex extension asks the upstream only for gzip, which Go's HTTP client decodes itself; today's core also advertises deflate, br and zstd.

When the client names no session, both cores derive a prompt cache key from the conversation's start so every turn of it shares the upstream's prompt cache; today's core hashes its own session identity (client key and canonical content), the new core's Codex extension the account, the model and the first developer and user messages. The values differ; each core's is stable across a conversation.
